ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the parabola $y=ax^2+bx+c$ ($a\ne 0$) has its vertex at point Q$(2, -1)$ and intersects the $y$-axis at point C$(0, 3)$ and intersects the $x$-axis at points A and B (with point A to the right of point B). Point P is a moving point on the parabola, moving from point C towards point A (point P does not coincide with A). A perpendicular line $PD\perp$ to line $AC$ is drawn at point P. If point P coincides with point Q, point E is on the $x$-axis, and point F is on the parabola, is there a parallelogram with vertices A, P, E, F? If it exists, write down the coordinates of point F directly; if not, please explain the reason.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the parabola opens upward, intersects the y-axis at point C, and intersects the x-axis at two points B and A, with A on the right side of B; the vertex Q is located below the x-axis. The left figure also draws point P on the parabola, and there is a line PD through P perpendicular to line AC; the right figure is a spare figure. The problem statement gives Q=(2,-1), C=(0,3), and when P coincides with Q, P=(2,-1). Reasoning: The vertex of the parabola is Q(2,-1), so set the parabola as y=a(x-2)^2-1. Substitute C(0,3), obtaining 3=4a-1, so a=1. Therefore the parabola is y=(x-2)^2-1=x^2-4x+3. Let y=0, obtaining x^2-4x+3=0, that is, x=1 or x=3. Because A is on the right side, A=(3,0). When P=Q, P=(2,-1). Let E=(t,0), and F=(x_F,y_F) be on the parabola. Since the problem only says A, P, E, F are vertices of a parallelogram, without fixing the order, it is necessary to use the equality of the midpoints of the diagonals to determine the possible pairings. The non-degenerate pairing that can make F not coincide with P and E not coincide with A is that A and E are one pair of opposite vertices, and P and F are another pair of opposite vertices, that is, A+E=P+F. Thus F=A+E-P=(3,0)+(t,0)-(2,-1)=(t+1,1). Because F is on the parabola, substitute y=1: 1=(x_F-2)^2-1. Also x_F=t+1, so 1=(t+1-2)^2-1=(t-1)^2-1, obtaining (t-1)^2=2. Therefore x_F=t+1=2±sqrt(2), and y_F=1. Hence such a parallelogram exists, and the coordinates of point F are (2-sqrt(2),1) or (2+sqrt(2),1).
